legacy_root.question: Implementation target: a canonical, closed vocabulary of mechanism ids with definitions and discriminating examples, replacing the free-text candidates[].mechanisms strings, so that mechanism-level deduplication becomes an exact set operation rather than a judgement call.
legacy_root.title: Define the canonical mechanism vocabulary that replaces free-text mechanism strings

mechanisms.definition: A fail-closed completeness gate: an empty or deleted guarded block is a failure, never a vacuous pass.
mechanisms.discriminating_example: Deleting the entire defaults block of a catalog while require_complete defaults false and CI passes no flag: the gate must go red, unlike a completeness check that is silent when zero rows remain.

mechanisms.definition: Provenance hashing of committed git blobs so a CRLF working copy cannot change a digest verdict.
mechanisms.discriminating_example: git cat-file -p HEAD:path returns LF bytes on Windows and Linux; hashing the working tree under core.autocrlf=true does not.

mechanisms.definition: Closed identifier namespace: every cited token resolves to exactly one record in one vocabulary.
mechanisms.discriminating_example: The M-NN option-id collision versus MECH-NN architecture cards: one literal token, two records.

mechanisms.definition: Blind independent first pass: each reader scores from a private source partition and must not see the other reader's notes or warrants.
mechanisms.discriminating_example: Two reviewers receive disjoint file partitions and are forbidden from reading each other's transcripts before scoring.

mechanisms.definition: Shared-context deliberation: later judges read earlier judges' transcripts or a common channel before scoring, so agreement can be echo rather than independent evidence.
mechanisms.discriminating_example: The second judge is handed the first judge's full transcript before scoring the same item.

mechanisms.definition: Deterministic replay: the same inputs plus a recorded seed must emit byte-identical artifacts on a second machine.
mechanisms.discriminating_example: Re-running the adapter with the recorded seed produces the same artifact bytes; any drift is a replay failure.

mechanisms.definition: Non-deterministic sampling: draws from a distribution (temperature, nucleus, or explicit RNG) so identical prompts need not yield identical completions.
mechanisms.discriminating_example: Raising temperature above zero yields different completions for one prompt across draws.

mechanisms.definition: Fire-and-forget dispatch: the parent spawns work and continues without joining; a background receipt is not a completion proof.
mechanisms.discriminating_example: The parent writes a background receipt and never waits for the child artifact; the join is discarded.

mechanisms.definition: Blocking fan-in barrier: the parent waits until every worker artifact exists and a shared reducer has judged the set.
mechanisms.discriminating_example: The parent blocks at a join until every worker file exists and the reducer runs; a missing artifact keeps the barrier red.

mechanisms.definition: Use-versus-mention: an artifact that documents a mechanism is not credited with implementing it.
mechanisms.discriminating_example: A handbook that describes fan-in barriers is not an implementation of a barrier.

mechanisms.definition: Source-anchor carriage: every IR node keeps its source anchor and licence class through translation, fusion, and rendering; an empty-string anchor is rejected as firmly as a missing one.
mechanisms.discriminating_example: Licence class stays attached to the IR node after fusion rewrites the tree; dropping the file:line anchor is a loss.

mechanisms.definition: Mechanism-level exact-set deduplication: two artifacts with the same canonical id set are the same mechanism set; prose similarity is not the operation.
mechanisms.discriminating_example: Two candidates with identical MX id sets collapse even when their free-text descriptions are rewritten.
